text:
oliver: Quick sync — span canonicalization cleanup and cost attribution migration. TL;DR: we still have three different span ids across services (span_id, legacy_span, upstream_span) and it’s blowing up joins for cost attribution. Want to align on a plan to converge and avoid rolling restarts for every service.

maya: +1. The biggest pain point is sampled traces losing billing_key during early sampling. If we push canonical_id later in pipeline we lose attribution for pre-sampled spans.

jen: I sketched a two-phase approach: 1) introduce canonical_span_id as an additive header propagated everywhere, keep legacy ids for reads, 2) update enrich pipeline to prefer canonical_span_id and copy billing_key to root envelope before sampling, 3) run a short backfill to populate canonical ids in archived traces and metrics links.

sam: Sounds reasonable. Two concerns: propagation size (headers growth) and rollout coordination. We should add a lightweight validation in the agent to avoid collisions. Also, we must ensure the per-tenant cost key is attached before any batching/sampling step.

oliver: Agree. Proposed invariants: \n- canonical_span_id must be idempotent (if present, services must not rewrite it).\n- billing_key must be set on the envelope root before any sampler or router sees it.\n- services that can’t produce canonical_span_id should copy legacy_span into canonical_span_id once, with a logged event so we can audit.

maya: For rollout, we can do a staged enable:\n- Stage A: agent emits X-Canonical-Span header (opt-in flag), enrich pipeline records it but still uses legacy_primary for joins.\n- Stage B: enrich pipeline starts emitting canonical_span_id in normalized envelope and we add attribute_mappings to downstream consumers.\n- Stage C: read-paths switch to canonical_span_id; after one week of stable metrics we drop legacy_primary.

jen: I wrote a quick envelope example we can use for staging: \n```\n{\n  "envelope_id": "env_..",\n  "tenant_id": "acme",\n  "billing_key": "billing:acct-123",\n  "canonical_span_id": "sp_abc123",\n  "legacy_span": "abc123",\n  "service": "payments",\n  "trace_sampled": true,\n  "payload": { ... }\n}\n```\nMake sure billing_key is at top-level.

sam: Nice. For collision checks we can validate canonical_span_id == legacy_span when services set it by copying; otherwise, if different, we log and drop the overwrite. Agent will emit a metric `canonical.overwrite_attempts`.

observability-bot: Note: there is an open alerting rule for missing billing_key in sampled envelopes. See #alerts/obs-missing-billing.

oliver: Ops checklist I propose: \n- SDK/agent: add X-Canonical-Span header + opt-in flag (owner: devex)\n- Enrich pipeline: copy billing_key to envelope root before sampling; accept canonical_span_id and index it (owner: eng-platform)\n- Backfill: one-time job to populate canonical_span_id for recent 30d traces (owner: eng-ml/research)\n- Read consumers: add mapping layer that falls back to legacy_span for 30d (owner: analytics)\n- Telemetry: create dashboards for canonical.overwrite_attempts and billing_key_missing_rate (owner: eng-sre)

maya: timeline? I can get SDK patch in 2 weeks, pipeline change in the next deploy window (3 weeks), backfill after we see stable metrics (target 5 weeks).

jen: For the backfill we should avoid re-ingesting raw traces. Instead, compute canonical_span_id = sha256(tenant_id||legacy_span||service) and write to a parallel table used by reads. Example SQL: \n```sql\nupdate trace_meta t\nset canonical_span_id = sha256(concat(t.tenant_id, t.legacy_span, t.service))\nwhere canonical_span_id is null and created_at > now() - interval '30 days';\n```\nThis keeps the write path cheap.

sam: One more tradeoff: if we derive canonical id deterministically for backfill, make sure runtime generation uses same algorithm to avoid mismatch. Document version in schema header (v1) so future changes are explicit.

oliver: Good catch. Add schema_version = "canonical_v1" to the envelope and to the backfill job.

jen: Questions for reviewers: do we allow services to opt-out of generating canonical_span_id and let pipeline generate it? That saves deploys but increases late-enrichment work.

maya: I prefer services generate it where possible. Fallback generation in pipeline only for legacy systems.

oliver: Decision (tentative): services should emit canonical_span_id when possible; pipeline will generate deterministic canonical ids as fallback. We'll run staged rollout with the opt-in header, monitor overwrite attempts and billing_key_missing_rate, then switch reads to canonical after stable window.

sam: I'll draft a short RFC for the rollout plan and include the metrics we need.

oliver: Thanks — @maya @jen @sam please ping if anything blocks. I’ll add the checklist to the eng-platform project board. :white_check_mark:
